_comment: Every constant the player-scale estimator uses. Nothing is hard-coded in the code; change a number here and rerun `run.py report` to see the effect. METHODOLOGY.md explains where each range comes from and how to challenge it.

ccu_to_dau.basis: Steam peak-concurrent to daily-unique ratio observed in published Valve/Steam Charts breakdowns and studio postmortems. Session-heavy competitive titles sit low, casual/mobile-style titles sit high.

dau_to_mau.basis: Inverse of typical DAU/MAU stickiness for games: 45% stickiness -> 2.2x, 22% -> 4.5x. Live-service shooters/MOBAs are stickier than gacha or single-player.

steam_share_of_pc.basis: Share of a Western PC title's players that are on Steam rather than Epic/EA app/Battle.net/standalone. Only applied when a title ships on Steam AND elsewhere.

platform_multipliers._comment: Applied to a PC-only signal (Steam CCU/owners) to reach the whole-IP audience. pc=1 by definition.

lifetime_to_mau._comment: Share of lifetime buyers/owners still playing in a given month, by game type. The single biggest lever in the whole model - this is where an 'estimate' really comes from.

registered_to_mau.basis: Registered accounts accumulate forever and include duplicates/bots. Treat as the weakest signal available.

freshness._comment: Confidence penalty for stale manual figures, applied to the half-width of the output range.

method_band._comment: Multiplicative half-width of the low/high band by method, before the freshness penalty.

ranking._comment: Kat's comment #2: rank Key IPs by sales AND by YouTube views. Scores are log10-scaled then min-max normalised inside the whole IP set, so one 1.5T-view outlier does not flatten everything else.

youtube._comment: search.list costs 100 quota units per call, videos.list/channels.list cost 1. See README for the quota budget.
